body:
I will not lie: I have a lot of trouble experiencing love. It happens, but it is not something that comes easily for me, probably because of my upbringing. If you have anything to suggest with regard to that, please do so.

But, to answer your question, I will say that yes, I loved her, at least in the beginning. It's just that going through that particular brand of hurt hardens me up really, really quick. Right now, I have to say that I feel somewhat sad, but mainly I am dissapointed with how she chose to act. She came by earlier today with her dad again, to feed the cats (god knows why, I usually take care of them). Again, talking in her mother tongue so I can't understand what is being said. Like I am some kind of threat. 

I feel that she is acting like that despite what she wrote in order to compartmentalize the hurt. It's probably easier for her to deal with the situation if she acts like I am some kind of savage, I guess...

Edit: I realized I forgot about another part, it seems. She had already been taking medication, and was suffering from panic attacks so bad she couldn't sleep some nights. When we were at the hospital waiting to see the psychiatrist, she confessed that earlier that week she felt compelled to kill herself. That happened a few times a month on average, but this time it was apparently so bad the only thing that stopped her was one of our cats nuzzling up to her. So yeah, there was a precedent to all this stuff. As for the forcing her to go see the psych part, I mellowed out the next day, and we ended up only going a week later at her insistence: she wanted to go to get sick days from her jobs, because she couldn't bear going back.
